explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - Biomni is an open-source Python library and CLI tool implementing a general-purpose biomedical AI agent (no dedicated frontend code in this repo).  
   - It orchestrates LLM calls, retrieval-augmented planning, domain-specific tools, and code execution to automate research tasks.

2. Analyze the file structure  
   - Top-level:  
     • setup.py, setup.cfg, MANIFEST.in → packaging/build configuration  
     • biomni_env/ → conda/R environment and CLI tools installation scripts  
     • biomni/ → core Python package  
     • tutorials/, fig/, figs/ → usage examples and assets  
   - Inside biomni/:  
     • agent/ → agent controllers (A1, planning, react framework)  
     • model/ → retrieval logic (Vector store, embeddings)  
     • task/ → abstract Task definition + domain-specific tasks  
     • tool/ → a registry of domain tools, schemas, and support utilities  
     • biorxiv_scripts/ → data-prep scripts for generating new tasks from preprints  
     • utils.py, llm.py, env_desc.py → cross-cutting utilities and LLM wrappers  
   - Patterns:  
     • Plugin/registry pattern in tool_registry.py  
     • Modular package structure (agent – model – tool – task)  
     • Separation of concerns: planning vs. execution vs. retrieval

3. Examine the README for additional insights  
   - Confirms core components: agent.go(), environment setup, tool/database integrations  
   - Emphasis on extensibility: add new tools, datasets, benchmarks  
   - Mentions Web UI separately (hosted outside this repo)

4. How to create the system design diagram  
   a. Main components:  
      • CLI / Python SDK layer (entry point)  
      • Agent Orchestrator (biomni.agent)  
      • LLM Interface (biomni.llm → OpenAI/Anthropic wrappers)  
      • Retrieval Engine (biomni.model.retriever + local data lake)  
      • Tool Registry & Domain Tools (biomni.tool + schema_db)  
      • Task Framework (biomni.task.*)  
      • Data Lake / Caches (~11 GB downloaded docs)  
      • Auxiliary Scripts (biomni/biorxiv_scripts)  
   b. Relationships & data flows:  
      • User → CLI/SDK → Agent  
      • Agent ↔ LLM Interface (prompts & responses)  
      • Agent ↔ Retrieval Engine (document search)  
      • Agent → Task modules (task definition & validation)  
      • Agent → Tool modules (domain-specific function calls)  
      • Tools ↔ Schema DB (pickle files)  
      • Scripts → populate Data Lake / generate tasks  
   c. Architectural patterns & design principles:  
      • Modular monolithic Python package with plugin registry for tools  
      • Separation of “planning” (LLM reasoning) vs. “execution” (tool calls)  
      • Retrieval-augmented pipeline (RAG) for grounding LLM in external docs  
      • Extensible: add new tools by registering in tool_registry  
   d. Key technologies/frameworks:  
      • Python 3.x, Conda environment management  
      • LLM APIs: OpenAI, Anthropic  
      • Vector store for embeddings (e.g., FAISS or similar)  
      • Pickle-based schema databases for domain knowledge  
      • Jupyter notebooks for tutorials

5. Tailoring the diagram for an open-source tool  
   - Highlight core library modules (biomni/) as central blocks  
   - Emphasize extension points: tool_registry and task definitions  
   - Show interaction with external systems (LLM APIs, data lake)  
   - Display script utilities for data ingestion (biorxiv_scripts)

6. Diagramming guidelines  
   - Use clear labels for each component block  
   - Connect blocks with directional arrows to show request/response and data flow  
   - Color-code or shape-code:  
     • Core engine (Agent, Model, Task)  
     • Extension points (Tools, Scripts)  
     • External systems (LLM API, Data Lake)  
   - Annotate arrows with protocols or data formats (e.g., “HTTP JSON”, “Pickle load”)

7. Emphasis on detail  
   - Include every module group (agent, model, tool, task, scripts)  
   - Show how new tools plug in via the registry  
   - Capture environment bootstrap (biomni_env) as a side process

By following these steps, the principal engineer can produce a detailed architectural diagram that faithfully represents Biomni’s modular, extensible AI agent design.
